Warranty-of-title/eviction suit over rural Texas land sold by act of sale; no dwelling-letting or lodging issue present.

holding_summary: A club had rented a lake-front 'camp' from its owner for several months; when a member helping remove property after the tenancy ended was injured by a rotten wharf stringer, the court held the owner liable, since a lessor is bound to know whether the premises he lets are safe and must answer in damages to anyone lawfully thereon injured by a defect, whether from original construction or failure to repair.

quotes.text: The owner is‘bound to know whether his building is safe for the purposes for which he rents it, or authorizes its use, or is rotten and unsafe, and is answerable, in damages, to those who, being lawfully therein, are injured by reason of its defects, whether of original construction or caused by failure to make proper repairs.

notes: The camp was rented April-June and then month-to-month for July-August (per opinion narrative), so occupancy is measured in months; the case affirms letting of a dwelling/camp as an ordinary incident of ownership carrying standard landlord liability, treated favorably as routine lawful practice rather than restricted.
Mandamus/injunction dispute over a restaurant-music permit ordinance; no lodging-house or dwelling-letting issue.
Food-standard ordinance (butter-fat content of ice cream/custard) struck down as arbitrary; unrelated to dwelling-letting or lodging regulation.

holding_summary: An elderly roomer who rented a room from defendant at $1 per week, and who fell after a defective door knob parted from the door, could not recover damages, because under ordinary Louisiana landlord-tenant law such minor repairs are by law the tenant's own responsibility, not the landlord's, even though she was unaware of the defect.

Streetcar one-man-car safety ordinance under police power; no dwelling-letting issue.

Parish cattle-tick-dipping ordinance under police power; unrelated to dwelling-letting.
Oyster-bedding-ground lease criminal statute construction; unrelated to dwelling-letting.

Tort suit by a lessee's wife against the landlord for injury from defective steps on a leased residence; addresses tort standing of non-lessee household members and the scope of C.C. arts. 2315/2322/670, not the compensated-occupancy practice, its short-term character, or its regulation -- an ordinary family residential lease with no duration or lodger facts given.
Homestead-exemption ownership/occupancy dispute; plaintiff had leased out the whole property, but the case concerns exemption law, not the legal character or regulation of letting.
